recipe_name: Wambatu Curry – Fried Brinjal with Coconut Milk
cooking_variation: Fried then simmered in spiced coconut gravy
recipe_description: Brinjal strips are fried until golden, then combined with tempered aromatics, spices, optional Maldive fish and a small quantity of coconut milk. Source yield is 2–3 servings.

recipe_name: Wambatu Curry / Brinjal Stew
recipe_description: A simple brinjal stew with curry powder, whole spices, coconut milk and water; the source specifies two servings.

recipe_name: Batu Moju
cooking_variation: Deep-fried and dressed in spiced vinegar-coconut mixture
recipe_description: A sweet-sour brinjal preparation with separately fried brinjal, onions and green chillies, then mixed with a spiced vinegar and coconut-milk dressing. Included as a distinct brinjal preparation, not labelled as an ordinary curry.

recipe_name: Sri Lankan Kukul Mas Curry – Embassy Recipe
cooking_variation: Marinated chicken with coconut milk and whole spices
recipe_description: Chicken pieces marinated with salt, pepper, garlic and chilli, then cooked with whole spices, curry powder, vinegar and coconut milk. Source says family of four.

recipe_name: Kukul Mas Curry – Roasted Spice Version
cooking_variation: Homemade roasted spice blend and coconut milk
recipe_description: Chicken curry using a homemade roasted spice powder, bone-in chicken and coconut milk. Source gives four servings and separate spice, chicken and curry ingredient groups.

recipe_name: Maalu Kirata – White Fish Curry with Coconut Milk
cooking_variation: Low-heat simmer in thin and thick coconut milk
recipe_description: Small fish or other fish for 3–4 people simmered with onion, green chilli, goraka, curry leaves and spices in thin coconut milk, then finished with thick coconut milk.

recipe_name: Ambul Thiyal – Sour Fish Curry
cooking_variation: Goraka and black pepper; no coconut milk in traditional version
recipe_description: Firm tuna or similar fish is marinated with vinegar or lime, goraka, salt and pepper, then simmered with aromatics and spices. Source includes coconut milk in its listed version; note this is not universal to traditional ambul thiyal.

recipe_name: Kiri Malu Curry – Sailfish Coconut Milk Curry
cooking_variation: Mild creamy curry with lime and whole spices
recipe_description: Sailfish cooked in coconut milk with onion, garlic, ginger, green chilli, curry leaves, pandan and a broad spice mix. The video description gives ingredient quantities and a cooking time but no serving yield.

recipe_name: Kiri Kos Maluwa – Mature Jackfruit Curry
recipe_description: Firm mature jackfruit bulbs (not sweet-ripe fruit) simmered in a mild golden coconut-milk gravy with curry leaves, pandan and gentle spices.

recipe_name: Kos Ata Kalu Pol Maluwa – Jackfruit Seed Curry
recipe_description: A traditional black-polkuru-style jackfruit seed curry. Source quantities are stated for 50 seeds; it does not state a serving yield, so per-person quantities are intentionally not calculated.

recipe_name: Sri Lankan Parippu Curry – Coconut Milk and Tempering
recipe_description: Red lentils are simmered with turmeric, pandan and curry leaves, then finished with thin and thick coconut milk and a separate onion-mustard temper.

recipe_name: Parippu Curry – Tempered Coconut Dhal
recipe_description: A multi-stage dhal preparation with a separate temper. The source gives ingredient quantities and steps but no explicit serving yield.

recipe_name: Polos Curry – Young Jackfruit Curry
recipe_description: Young green jackfruit is simmered slowly with roasted Sri Lankan curry powder, coconut milk and souring agent until tender and dark. Source gives four servings and approximately 45–60 minutes simmering before final reduction.

recipe_name: Ala Kiri Hodi (Creamy Coconut-Milk Potato Curry)
recipe_description: Potato pieces simmered in a mild turmeric and coconut-milk gravy with onion, garlic, green chilli, curry leaves and pandan. The defining feature is a creamy, relatively mild gravy rather than a dry fried finish.

recipe_name: Ala Hodi (Everyday Potato Curry)
recipe_description: An everyday Sri Lankan potato curry in which potatoes and aromatics cook together in coconut milk. The source describes a low-to-medium heat simmer until the potatoes are cooked and the gravy thickens.

recipe_name: Ala Thel Dala (Sri Lankan Potato Fry)
recipe_description: A dry potato side dish made by boiling potatoes until fork-tender, then mixing them with caramelised onion, green chilli, chilli flakes, turmeric, pepper, Maldive fish, curry leaves, pandan and cinnamon.

recipe_name: Devilled Potatoes (Ala Thel Dala – SBS Version)
recipe_description: A devilled Sri Lankan potato preparation using parboiled potato cubes tossed with onion, green chilli, curry leaves, mustard seeds, garlic, Maldive fish, chilli flakes, turmeric and tomato.

recipe_name: Potato Tempered (Pulse Recipe)
recipe_description: A dry tempered potato dish in which potato cubes are fried until lightly golden, then mixed with onion, green chilli, garlic, turmeric, salt, chilli flakes, Maldive fish, curry leaves and pandan.

recipe_name: Wattakka Maluwa – Coconut Milk and Roasted Coconut Paste
cooking_variation: Roasted coconut paste / kalu pol style
recipe_description: Mature pumpkin simmered in coconut milk and finished with a toasted coconut, mustard, raw-rice and spice paste. The source describes this as the traditional roasted-paste version.

recipe_name: Wattakka Kalu Pol Maluwa
recipe_description: A darker pumpkin curry using dry-roasted spices and browned coconut-rice paste; the source gives an approximate yield of 2–3 servings.
